terms.gloss: sing to deaf ears: talk in vain
evidence: Verg. Ecl. 10.8: nōn canimus surdīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The deaf ears stand in the dative, with no preposition.
Traupman’s form, with ad; not found as a phrase in Lewis & Short or the Latinitas loci collections, so Traupman is the only evidence.

phrases.latin: quae vereor nē vāna surdīs auribus cecinerim
phrases.english: which I fear I have sung in vain to deaf ears

sources: Lewis & Short: surdus · Lewis & Short: cano
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 96, checked against the searchable text and the page images of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
